newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIAN EXOTICS - Thai baht dips, regionals jittery.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN EXOTICS - Thai baht dips, regionals jittery.

text.p: The Thai baht fell sharply in Asia, triggering a wave of dollar hedging against other regionals after the resignation of Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan, dealers said on Thursday.
"The resignation news helped the dollar rise against most currencies, except the Sing dollar," a U.S. investment house dealer said, adding that investors were losing confidence.
He said the dollar was likely to benefit for a while from the chaos in Thailand, although tight supply of baht offshore would limit dollar/baht gains as it limits short-selling.
The baht was pushed down to 26.300 against the dollar in the late morning, but revived to 25.150/650 at midday.
Dollar/baht was at 25.850/25.880 late on Wednesday.
Some dealers said news that Commerce Minister Narongchai Akrasanee also planned to tender his resignation would prompt further selling of baht.
The Bank of Thailand set the mid-rate at 25.77 baht to the dollar against 25.76 on Wednesday, dealers said.
In Malaysia, the ringgit was dented by early dollar demand, a continuation of Wednesday's short covering, but rises were seen capped at 2.5160/70.
The ringgit was seen defensive due to lingering concerns about Malaysia's poor trade data -- a deficit of 2.1 billion ringgit for April after a 1.75 billion ringgit surplus in March.
At 0430 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.5170/80 against a close of 2.5142/52 on Wednesday.
A U.S. bank dealer said dollar/ringgit could test the next barrier at 2.5200 and possibly make a minor break to 2.5220.
The Singapore dollar experienced quiet trade as traders stayed sidelined ahead of Friday's May non-oil export data, which are likely to be in positive territory.
A Reuter poll of 10 financial institutions predicted on average a 3.5 percent growth in nominal terms year-on-year, but some economists said that would not signal a robust turnaround.
Dealers said the Sing dollar was supported by unrest in the regionals, a result of baht volatility, but a mixed outlook for Singapore's electronics sector could puncture its silver lining.
At 0430 GMT, dollar/Sing was at 1.4247/57, a notch firmer than its opening levels but holding steady in a 1.42/1.43 range.
The Indonesian rupiah continued to trade sluggishly amid adequate liquidity conditions, and with an eye on the baht.
Dealers said the dollar was also gaining against the rupiah due to short covering ahead of the weekend, although rises were seen fairly well resisted at 2,430.
Spot rupiah was at 2,430.70/1.70 at 0430 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,427.5/28.5.
Dealers said fears of a swap squeeze similar to Thailand's continued to linger in the forward market with swap rates rising.
Many tended to hold onto long forward positions although intervention by the central bank was not likely, dealers said.
-- Syed Azman in Kuala Lumpur (603-206 2323), Mantik Kusjanto in Jakarta (6221 384-6364), Anuchit Nguyen in Bangkok (662) 652-0642 and Jacqueline Wong in Singapore (65-8703090)
